header.title: TIGERS-X experiment cube
header.lead: Technical limits, interfaces, and safety results for integrating an experiment with the TIGERS-X platform. The page brings together the product specification and the Payload User's Guide, version 1.1 (April 2026), prepared by the ISHA and ARSL research teams.
sources: Product specification, including the CRS-34 flight record.

overview.title: Overview
paragraphs: The user's guide is the reference for researchers and experiment developers. It states the technical specifications, interface boundaries, and operational constraints for flying an experiment inside TIGERS-X.

TIGERS-X is a 2U × 2U experiment cube for the ICE Cubes Facility on the International Space Station. It runs autonomous microfluidic mixing experiments, films them with four cameras, and downlinks data in near real time.
overview.identityCaption: Identity and flight record, from the product specification.

identity.label: Full name
identity.value: Thailand Innovative G-force Varied Emulsification Research for Space Exploration

identity.label: Host platform
identity.value: ICE Cubes Facility, Columbus module, ISS

identity.label: Primary application
identity.value: Passive mixing and emulsion stability of medical fluids

identity.label: Flight
identity.value: Launched on SpaceX CRS-34, 15 May 2026 (US time). Returned on CRS-34 Dragon, splashdown 17 June 2026.

features: 2U × 2U cube, 200 × 200 × 100 mm, with a 2.5 kg experiment mass budget.
Sequences run on board. Ground commanding is through the ICE Cubes Mission Control Centre.
Two-tier computing: an Orange Pi 5 Ultra for processing and data handling, and an STM32F7 microcontroller for low-level hardware control.
Four global-shutter RGB and IR cameras in a 2 × 2 array, with overlapping fields of view and hardware H.264 recording.
Optional microfluidic module: eight peristaltic pumps, sealed fluid bags, and 4-channel static-mixer chips.
One DB13W3P connector carries +12 V power and the LAN data link. The shell is bonded to the frame.
IPv4 over TCP/HTTPS through a VPN, YAMCS telemetry, and SFTP file downlink.
Designed to MIL-STD-461G EMC tests and ISS crew-safety standards (SSP and JSC).

mechanical.title: Mechanical
mechanical.intro: The cube integrates with the host facility in a 2 × 2U form factor. Dimensions are in millimetres.
mechanical.envelopeCaption: Envelope and mass. Both documents are cited where the limits differ.

envelope.label: Maximum experiment mass
envelope.value: 2.5 kg in the user's guide. The product specification allows up to 3 kg.

envelope.label: Maximum equivalent vent radius
envelope.value: About 300 cm. The product specification cites an ISS limit of 5080 cm. The user's guide describes the value as well within an ISS maximum of ≪ 5080 cm.

mechanical.partsCaption: Parts list from the mechanical drawing.

electrical.title: Electrical
electrical.connectorAlt: DB13W3 connector face. Large contacts are labeled A3, A2, and A1. The upper signal pins are labeled 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 and the lower pins 10, 9, 8, 7, 6.
electrical.intro: The power system supplies regulated power to the experimental subsystems. The primary input is +12 V DC through a DB13W3P mixed-layout connector. The connector shell is bonded to the structural frame for grounding. Regulated 5 V and 3.3 V rails are available for the payload.
electrical.phasesIntro: The user's guide requires the payload to stay inside these phases.
electrical.phasesCaption: Power phases from the user's guide.
electrical.limitsCaption: Shared limits from both documents. Current and temperature maxima are given from each source.

limits.label: Input current
limits.max: 1.8 A in the user's guide. 3.1 A in the product specification.

limits.label: Internal temperature
limits.max: 45 °C in the user's guide. Up to 40 °C in the product specification.

imaging.title: Imaging
imaging.figureAlt: View of the imaging assembly: the camera hardware that records the experiment.
imaging.intro: Onboard diagnostics record the experiment. Processing and camera control are split across two computers.

processing.label: Main computer
processing.value: Orange Pi 5 Ultra, 16 GB RAM, 64 GB eMMC, 1 TB NVMe SSD

processing.label: Microcontroller
processing.value: STM32F746VIT6, 1 MB flash, 320 KB SRAM, for low-level hardware control

camera.label: Array
camera.value: 4 cameras in a 2 × 2 matrix, with overlapping fields of view

camera.label: Sensor
camera.value: See3CAM_27CUG, 2 megapixel global shutter, 1600 × 1300, RGB and IR

camera.label: Recording
camera.value: Hardware H.264 in an MP4 container, 4000 kbit/s

data.title: Data and command
data.figureAlt: View of the electronics that handle data and commanding.
data.intro: Power and data share the DB13W3P connector. An internal LAN port carries IPv4 over TCP/HTTPS through a secure VPN. Files are downlinked by SFTP. The Orange Pi 5 Ultra manages telemetry and the bulk transfer.
data.path: YAMCS server in the experiment cube, then the ICE Cubes Facility, the ISS Control Centre, the ICE Cubes Mission Control Centre (ICMCC), and finally the archive and Open MCT display.
data.bulk: About 1.8 GB takes about 240 minutes at 1 Mbit/s, and about 480 minutes at a degraded 0.5 Mbit/s.

fluidics.title: Fluidic system
fluidics.intro: An optional microfluidic module is available for biological or chemical experiments. The product specification notes that the mixer can be modified.
fluidics.pumps: Eight peristaltic pumps. The user's guide names them Tagasako RP-QIII.
fluidics.storageAlt: View of the fluid storage bags.
fluidics.storage: 10 ml sealed storage bags. The product specification allows bags up to 20 ml. The user's guide states 10 ml secure storage bags.
fluidics.mixerAlt: View of the microfluidic static mixer, with four channels on the chip.
fluidics.mixer: Microfluidic static mixer, 4 channels per chip.

safety.title: Qualification and safety
safety.intro: TIGERS-X is qualified to the MIL-STD-461G EMC tests below and to the listed ISS crew-safety standards. The sealed container holds 64.59 J against a 19,307 J limit.

emc.description: Conducted emissions, audio-frequency currents, power leads
Conducted emissions, radio-frequency potential, power leads

safety.crewIntro: Results below are those recorded in the product specification, with the sharper wording from the user's guide kept where it adds a limit. A dash means the documents cite the standard and do not state a separate result.
safety.crewCaption: ISS safety hazards, standards, and payload results.

hazards.hazard: Crew eye safety, UV and incoherent light above 10,000 nits
Battery leakage or rupture, low-BRC cells
Material offgassing in the habitable volume

hazards.result: Toxicity Hazard Level 0 or N/A. Biological Safety Level ≤ 1

hazards.hazard: Sharp particles from glass or frangible parts
hazards.result: Parts enclosed, with positive protection against release of particles larger than 50 µm
No safety violations identified, and no safety impact

hazards.standard: SSP 30237 and SSP 30243, or COL-ESA-RQ-014 and/or OE-14-002

hazards.result: Kinetic energy below 19,307 J (14,240 ft-lb). Not fracture critical

hazards.standard: ISS limits: stored energy below 19,307 J, and ΔP ≤ 1.52 bar
hazards.result: 64.59 J stored energy. Maximum ΔP 1.12 bar
